request.spec:
While an as-of date is set, the roles shown on the screen are those in force at the end of that
day.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
While an as-of date is set, the roles shown on the screen are those in force at the end of that
day.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
All 4 tests in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts` now pass under `bin/e2e`.

**The as-of roles change was already built.** Before I changed anything, the main "as of roles" test and scenarios 1 and 2 passed. The as-of view (`AsOfView.settings`) already works out each user's role from the role history, as it stood at the end of the chosen day. So nothing was needed for roles.

**Scenario 3 failed on something else.** In that test, a person has their own payment terms (3 days) dated from 2026-03-01. They are then edited with the terms field blank and no from-date. The test expects that edit's audit line to end in `terms=3`. The server treated it as no change to the terms and left `terms=` off the line.

**My one change is in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/person/Person.java` (`editTerms`).** A save that leaves the terms blank now counts as a terms change when dated terms are in force on the sheet's today. The audit line then shows the terms still in force (`terms=3`). In every other case the existing rule stands: a save giving the terms the person already had changes nothing.

**Decision for you:** this partly goes against a comment in the code, which said such a save "changes nothing, even while dated terms are in force". I followed the test and kept the exception narrow (blank terms only), and updated the comment to say so. If the code's original rule is the one you want, the test's expected audit line would need to change instead.
